studies.title: Labouring Toward A Meeting
studies.meaning: The verb chosen for a human life is one of hard, wearing labour, and it is doubled for emphasis. You are toiling toward your Lord, toiling, and you will meet Him. Then two cases, and only the first is completed here. A record handed to the right hand, an easy reckoning, and a return to family in gladness. The second case is left hanging at the end of the unit, with the book arriving from behind.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, from a short surah that opens with the sky tearing and the earth being flattened and emptied. No specific occasion is reported for these ayat. The address turns to the individual immediately after the scene, which is the pattern of several surahs in this part of the Quran: a cosmic event described in three lines, then one person named and questioned.

keyTerms.note: A word for effort that leaves a mark, used of scratching or wearing a surface down. It describes work that costs the worker something, and it is applied here to every human life without exception.

The phrase pairs the accounting word with the word for what is light. The classical readers describe it as a review rather than an examination, an account presented and passed over rather than argued.

A doubled expression, behind and back together, so the position is emphasised. The classical readers describe an arm brought round from behind, which makes receiving the record itself part of the difficulty.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Everyone in that world worked with their body. Water was carried, grain was ground by hand, and a caravan journey meant weeks of walking beside animals. A word for labour that wears a person down was not a metaphor to that audience; it was the description of an ordinary day. Setting a whole life inside that word tells a listener what kind of thing living is, using vocabulary he had earned.
studies.didYouKnow: The classical collections preserve an exchange about this exact phrase. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that anyone examined closely in the reckoning is ruined, and was asked about this ayah's promise of an easy account. He answered that the easy one is a presentation, and that being argued with is the ruin.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The passage makes effort universal and destination optional. Everyone is described as labouring toward the same meeting; what differs is what the labour produced. That removes idleness as a possibility: nobody in the description is standing still. The detail about returning to family is also worth noticing, since the reward described first is not a garden but going back to the people you belonged to, in a good mood.

crossReferences.why: Shows the same moment at greater length, with the recipient handing his record round to be read.
Finishes the sentence this unit leaves open, giving the outcome for the record received from behind.
Adds what happens with the record afterwards, the person made to read it against himself.

studies.applyIt: Notice how much of today was actual effort and how much was motion. The ayah says everyone is labouring, so the question is not whether you worked but what the work was aimed at. Pick one hour tomorrow and give it to something you would be content to find on a record, then let the rest of the day be ordinary.
